newsitem.title: CHINA: Dragonair plans major upgrade of Airbus fleet.
newsitem.headline: Dragonair plans major upgrade of Airbus fleet.

text.p: Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd (Dragonair) said on Thursday it is upgrading its Airbus fleet and could more than double its size in the next four years.
From February 1998, the airline will start replacing its seven leased Airbus A320-200s with new leased A320s, Dragonair chief executive Stanley Hui said.
It also has orders or options to lease further A320s from International Lease Finance Corp, or to buy further aircraft, including an A330-300, from Airbus Industrie, he said.
It also retains the option of swapping two A320s for larger A321 aircraft in future, Hui said.
"If all our options ... are exercised, Dragonair's fleet could very easily grow to 15 A320s and six A330s by the beginning of the next century," Hui told a news conference.
"That would mean that Dragonair will have more than doubled in size in just four years," Hui said.
All of its new A320s will use new V2500-A5 engines, and Dragonair has ordered or has options to buy more V2500-A5s, he said.
The upgrade was Dragonair's biggest investment ever, but Hui declined to put a figure on the transaction's value.
However, based on new list prices, all orders and options to buy -- including options to buy -- would amount to about HK$3.5 billion, Hui said.
Hui also said Dragonair was "in a very liquid financial situation" and had no timetable for a flotation."
Asked if there was disagreement among Dragonair shareholders about a flotation, Hui said: "The shareholders are working together very closely with one common objective."
CITIC Pacific Ltd owns 28 percent of Dragonair, and Swire Pacific Ltd and Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd jointly hold 26 percent of Dragonair.
